answer.location_description: A thin horizontal band spanning the full image width near the top edge, rows 2-3. This is far from the centred nodule, in the lung or chest-wall periphery of the crop.
answer.shortcut_type: bright horizontal line / stripe artifact near top edge
answer.mechanism:
Two families of structured first-layer units read rows 2-3 with opposite signs.

'Benign' family (units 2, 5, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, 25, 29, 30; large positive biases):
- Weights of about +20 to +60 across all 24 columns of rows 2-3.
- Weaker or negative weights in the flanking rows 4-5.
- So these units act as a line detector.

'Malignant' family (units 3, 8, 21, 24, 27, 28; negative biases):
- Weights of about -20 to -50 across rows 2-3.
- Positive weights (+20 to +45) in rows 4-5.
- So a bright line at rows 2-3 suppresses them.

Propagated through layers 2 and 3 (ignoring ReLU gating), each family has a clear net effect on the logit:
- Unit 2 has a net effect of about -22,500 (integer units), which is strongly toward benign.
- Unit 3 has a net effect of about +21,000, toward malignant. Unit 20 is about +8,900, also toward malignant.

A bright stripe at rows 2-3 therefore both raises the benign units and lowers the malignant units. Both changes push the logit negative, toward benign.
answer.evidence:
Rows 2-3 carry uniform full-width weights of consistent sign within each family. For example:
- Unit 14 row 2: 39 9 8 48 21 0 29 18 55 54 ...
- Unit 19 row 3: 40 46 34 34 28 31 28 41 47 ...
- Unit 27 row 2: -31 -25 -17 -30 -5 -37 -45 ...
- Unit 28 row 3: -25 -38 -22 -8 -19 ...

This full-width uniformity is unlike the radially organised nodule weights in the centre of the same units. The pattern is a sign flip between rows 2-3 and rows 4-5 (unit 3: row 2 about -40, row 4 about +30), not a ring that fades with distance from the centre. A real nodule- or lung-centred feature would not produce a sharp, edge-to-edge band at a fixed row near the border.

Layer-2 to output contributions: benign-family unit 2 maps to the logit at about -22.5k (integer units); malignant-family unit 3 at about +21k.

Weaker horizontal banding also appears at rows 18-23, so the exact location carries some uncertainty.
answer.main_feature: Nodule size and compactness around the image centre. Units with a positive centre and a negative surrounding ring (rows 8-17), i.e. small, well-circumscribed bright nodules, push toward benign. Units with a negative centre and positive weights in a wider annulus (rows 6-17), i.e. larger nodules whose brightness extends outward, push toward malignant.
